transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-15
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Jordan Kim (Redwood SE); Marcus Lee (Acme - Head of ML); Diana Flores (Acme - Platform Eng); Ravi Patel (Acme - CISO); Sara Gomez (Acme - Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Console walkthrough focused on per-route dashboards and cost. Demoed token-level breakdowns and routing policies. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and security controls (KMS, audit logs).

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Alex with Redwood, AE. With me is Priya and Jordan, our SEs. How are you doing Marcus?
[00:00:10] Marcus Lee: Good, thanks. We got a few folks on from infra and security. We are really interested in how you show cost per product route and how to attribute spend back to feature teams.
[00:00:20] Diana Flores: Yeah want to see the per-route analytics and how you measure token consumption per endpoint.
[00:00:25] Alex Chen: Perfect, that's exactly what we planned to cover. We'll jump into the Console and show our usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then the cost breakdown — token-level and route-level. We'll also touch on routing policies and Dedicated vs Hosted briefly.
[00:00:40] Priya Nair: I'll share my screen — give me a sec — ok can you all see the Redwood Console? (background typing noises)
[00:00:50] Sara Gomez: Yep we can see it, looks clean.
[00:00:55] Priya Nair: Great. This is the account overview — topline usage for the last 30 days, token consumption, and cost. On the right we have per-route cards. Each route is a logical endpoint you define in your app, e.g., /chat, /summarize, /embeddings.
[00:01:15] Marcus Lee: Can you filter by team or tag? We have multiple squads hitting the same model but need per-team cost backfills.
[00:01:22] Priya Nair: Yes, routes can be tagged with metadata. You can filter by tag, team, or API key. We also have a CSV export so finance can ingest the per-route breakdown.
[00:01:35] [00:01:35] (transcription glitch: "routes" read as "roots")
[00:01:40] Jordan Kim: Drilling into an individual route — here's /checkout-chat — you can see qps, p95 latency, and token distribution (prompt vs completion). Down below is a time-series of cost per hour and per-day token delta.
[00:01:58] Diana Flores: Where does the token cost come from? Is that a raw multiply by model rate or do you apply any caching/batching credits?
[00:02:05] Priya Nair: Good question — by default the Console computes cost as tokens * model unit price based on your pricing plan. We also surface an "effective cost" that factors in cache hits and batching savings if you enable our Optimize suggestions. So you'll see an adjustment line when prefix caching or batching is active.
[00:02:24] Marcus Lee: That sounds useful. For us, embeddings are huge — can you break down which routes are embeddings heavy vs generation heavy?
[00:02:31] Priya Nair: Yup, the route-level view has a model usage pie and a token-type stack: embeddings, prompt, completion. You can toggle to see model versions and quantized vs fp16 variants.
[00:02:45] Ravi Patel: On security — we need exact logs for audit. How granular are your audit logs? SSO for RBAC? And KMS for keys?
[00:02:55] Alex Chen: We do RBAC with SSO/SAML, and audit logs at the request level with metadata (route, API key, model version). For Private/Dedicated deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; for hosted we provide optional envelope encryption + key rotation integrations with external KMS.
[00:03:14] Sara Gomez: Can you redacted PII in logs?
[00:03:18] Jordan Kim: We have log redaction rules and retention policies configurable per-tenant. For PII we recommend not storing plain requests and use our masking preprocessor or route-specific redaction.
[00:03:31] Marcus Lee: Back to costs — can you show an example of a multi-route cost allocation for a single user journey?
[00:03:35] Priya Nair: Sure — here's a Journey view: product flows mapped to routes with stacked cost attribution. For user checkout flow, it shows 35% cost in embeddings (search), 50% in generation (confirmation copy), 15% misc. You can export per-request traces to see exact tokens for each step.
[00:03:55] [00:03:55] (small crosstalk, inaudible)
[00:04:05] Diana Flores: How accurate are the token counts? We have our own tokenizer and sometimes there are small diffs.
[00:04:12] Priya Nair: We report tokenization based on the model tokenizer configured for that model family, but we can ingest your tokenizer mapping if you want exact parity. Typically differences are within a few percent.
[00:04:25] Marcus Lee: If we pin a model version or switch to a quantized profile, do you show the historical impact on latency and cost?
[00:04:33] Jordan Kim: Yes, each model rollout record shows before/after metrics — tokens, cost, latency p50/p95 and quality regressions linked to eval prompt sets. You can roll back or configure automatic fallback to a previous variant.
[00:04:50] Ravi Patel: For Dedicated, what's the SLA and can we reserve capacity for peak windows?
[00:04:56] Alex Chen: Dedicated has commit tiers with guaranteed capacity and SLAs up to 99.9% uptime depending on tier. You can config autoscale policies and burst capacity. We'll include sample policies in the follow-up docs.
[00:05:10] Marcus Lee: We need to justify spend to finance — do you have per-feature showbacks that map to our internal cost centers?
[00:05:17] Priya Nair: Yes — we support tagging and mapping to cost centers. The Console has a Cost Allocation page where you can assign routes or API keys to cost centers and generate monthly reports.
[00:05:28] Sara Gomez: How does Optimize fit in — you mentioned batching suggestions earlier.
[00:05:33] Priya Nair: Redwood Optimize analyzes your traffic patterns and suggests batching windows, cache TTLs, and model/quantization recommendations per workload. In the Console we surface a "Savings estimate" per suggestion so you can see projected cost reduction and impact on latency.
[00:05:48] Marcus Lee: What's the risk of quality regressions if we quantize? Do you have guardrails?
[00:05:52] Jordan Kim: We run continuous evals against your eval set and flag regressions. In the dashboard you can compare outputs and accept/reject suggestions. Also we integrate automated A/B rollouts so only a subset of traffic uses the quantized variant for a period.
[00:06:10] Diana Flores: Ok show me the per-route anomaly detection — we need alerts if cost spikes.
[00:06:15] Priya Nair: Here's alerts — you can set thresholds on token count, cost per hour, or latency p95. Alerts can post to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook. We also have anomaly detection that uses historical seasonality to detect unusual spikes and suggests investigating specific API keys or routes.
[00:06:33] Marcus Lee: Great. Can we correlate logs to traces? Like go from an alert to the exact request sample?
[00:06:38] Jordan Kim: Yes, the alert links to a filtered timeline and per-request traces. Note that request payloads may be redacted depending on retention and PII rules.
[00:06:48] [00:06:48] (short pause)
[00:06:55] Ravi Patel: On compliance — do you have SOC 2 Type II? ISO? And do you provide a customer-specific audit package?
[00:07:02] Alex Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II; we also have ISO 27001 in progress. For enterprise customers we provide SOC 2 artifacts through an NDA and can include platform architecture diagrams, penetration test summaries, and KMS/HSM integration details.
[00:07:20] Marcus Lee: We have a question about request routing — can you route by latency vs cost? For example, route lower-priority traffic to cheaper region or model variant?
[00:07:28] Priya Nair: Absolutely. Smart routing policies let you prioritize by latency SLO or cost. You can define rules that route to cheaper model variants or a lower-cost region for non-critical requests, and set automatic fallback to a higher tier for errors.
[00:07:43] Diana Flores: Does routing add significant complexity to instrumentation? We want unified metrics.
[00:07:48] Jordan Kim: Routing is transparent in the Console — you still get a unified view of metrics but can slice by route, region, or policy. Each request logs the selected path and model so you can audit it.
[00:07:59] Marcus Lee: Performance wise — can we run a small synthetic benchmark to validate p95 with our payloads?
[00:08:05] Alex Chen: Yes, we recommend running a short POC benchmark with your representative prompts. We'll provision a burst capacity and run against your sample workload — Priya can coordinate exporting the per-route analytics after the test.
[00:08:16] Priya Nair: I'll note that. We'll need a sample prompt set and expected qps. For embeddings heavy flows, we may suggest batching or a dedicated embedding pool.
[00:08:27] Sara Gomez: Any hidden fees? Network egress?
[00:08:30] Alex Chen: Core pricing is tokens + reserved compute for Dedicated. Network egress is generally covered but can be accounted separately for Private/on-prem setups. We'll send the pricing sheet that outlines everything.
[00:08:41] Marcus Lee: Ok let's talk timeline — we'd like to have a pilot by early December. Is that feasible?
[00:08:46] Alex Chen: Yes, pilot in early December is reasonable. We'll send over contract terms and sample timelines in the follow-up.
[00:08:55] [00:08:55] (minor transcription glitch: "contract" heard as "con tract")
[00:09:00] Priya Nair: Quick demo highlight — here's a per-route cost breakdown for the last 30 days. You can see tokens, effective cost after Optimize savings, and percentage of total spend. Clicking into the route shows the top 10 consumers (API keys/users) and a per-request sample.
[00:09:20] Diana Flores: Can we programmatically pull these metrics into our internal dashboard?
[00:09:23] Jordan Kim: Yes — we have a Metrics API and an S3 CSV export. Many customers pull daily exports into finance systems.
[00:09:30] Marcus Lee: For the CSV, can you include tags and cost center mappings?
[00:09:33] Priya Nair: Yep, those columns are included. We'll attach an example export.
[00:09:40] Sara Gomez: Anything else on security we should be aware of?
[00:09:44] Ravi Patel: One more — key rotation policy. We need automatic rotation and ability to revoke keys quickly.
[00:09:50] Alex Chen: We support key rotation and revocation via KMS for Private/Dedicated. For hosted we have scheduled rotation and emergency revoke with notification hooks.
[00:10:05] Marcus Lee: Great. Ok can we do a quick recap and next steps?
[00:10:10] Alex Chen: Sure. Recap: demoed Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, token-level cost and Optimize suggestions. Action items: we'll send pricing and SOC2/security deck; Priya will share per-route CSV; customer will provide sample prompt sets and compliance requirements. Set POC check-in week of 11/24.
[00:10:30] Diana Flores: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:10:33] Marcus Lee: Thanks — looking forward to the docs.
[00:10:36] Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with notes and attachments.
[00:10:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-words and filler, some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (e.g., KMS sometimes separated), timestamps approximate.
